propositions: Creating a ticket directory with os.makedirs outside the write lock, then writing the first event file inside the lock, leaves a window where process interruption strands an empty orphaned directory visible to fsck as MISSING_CREATE and FOREIGN_STORE_PATH.

Staging the directory and its first event file together in a dot-prefixed temporary path (.tmp-newticket-*-*), then publishing both atomically via os.rename under the write lock, prevents orphaned empty ticket directories from being visible to fsck scanners.

The same vulnerable mkdir-then-write pattern exists in batch_stage_and_commit, inbound_translate._write_event_file, and dispatch_one BRIDGE_ALERT emission; all must be converted to use the staging-then-promote pattern to close the debris window across the entire store write path.

Stale staging directories from dead writer processes (identified by host+pid-namespace+start-time stamp) are cleaned up on writer startup with bounded, best-effort sweep, without violating the 043f rule that reader-side cleanup of event-less ticket directories is forbidden.
The atomic directory+event publication happens under the existing write lock and after rebase guard and under_lock_check, so event visibility and concurrency semantics are unchanged from before.
